findings.title: Test suite requires WORKSPACE_MANAGER_REQUIRE_SANITIZER=false but conftest does not export it
findings.description: Running `pytest fabric/workspace-manager/tests/ -v` directly (without setting WORKSPACE_MANAGER_REQUIRE_SANITIZER=false) fails 44 tests with ImportError because the production-hard-fail kicks in. The fix commit message claims '72/72 pass' but this is only true when the env var is exported externally. conftest.py should set os.environ.setdefault('WORKSPACE_MANAGER_REQUIRE_SANITIZER', 'false') (or use monkeypatch at session scope) so CI runs work out of the box without operator knowledge. This is a developer-experience issue, not a security regression: the production default remains hard-fail.
findings.impact: CI pipelines or new contributors running the suite without the env var see misleading ImportError failures; could mask real regressions if someone disables the check incorrectly.
findings.recommendation: Add `os.environ.setdefault('WORKSPACE_MANAGER_REQUIRE_SANITIZER', 'false')` near the top of conftest.py (before any imports of logging_setup or main), or set it in pyproject.toml's [tool.pytest.ini_options] env section.
